newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: MOTORCYCLING-OKADA GETS POLE POSITION IN MALAYSIA GRAND PRIX.
newsitem.headline: MOTORCYCLING-OKADA GETS POLE POSITION IN MALAYSIA GRAND PRIX.

text.p: Japan's Tadayuki Okada confirmed his pole position for the 500cc race in Sunday's Malaysian Grand Prix by clocking the best time in the second practice session on Saturday.
The Honda rider clocked a best time of one minute 23.485 seconds after also having the fastest time on Friday.
Tadayuki broke the record of 1:25.100 set at the 3.505-km Shah Alam circuit by American John Kocinski in 1991.
Reigning world champion Michael Doohan of Australia took second position for Sunday's race with a best time of 1:23.904.
Doohan, who also rides a Honda, has had a slow warm-up for the opening race of the season and managed only fourth position in Friday's practice.

"I missed a gear and had to go into a corner too deep to compensate for the error. So it was really my fault that I missed out on the chance to get pole," the Australian said after Saturday's practice.
Japan's Nobuatsu Aoki, another Honda rider, will start in the third position while Alex Criville of Spain will take the fourth slot in his Yamaha.
Italy's Massimiliano Biaggi took pole position for the 250cc by clocking 1:25.380 on his Honda.
Fellow Italian Valentino Rossi, an Aprilia rider, will start first in the 125cc after clocking 1:30.720 in practice.
